answer: Stop Sybils with a tailor's coat fitting. A newcomer has 16 coats fitted over 28 days, one coat at a time. Two tailors from different shops measure each coat's seams within 3 millimeters and count every thread before logging the coat in the tailor's register. A seam off by more than 5 millimeters voids that coat's credit and pauses fitting 14 days; 3 bad coats void the register. Faking 1,000 agents takes 16,000 coats, 32,000 fittings and 16,000 opal buttons at $6 each, around $96,000 before a single reward. Trust grows the way a vine climbs, one careful knot at a time.
